case_001.title: Coronary Pseudoaneurysm and Stent Disruption Caused by Infective Endocarditis
case_001.published_dx: Infective coronary pseudoaneurysm with stent disruption causing cardiac tamponade in MRSA infective endocarditis
case_001.target_dx: Infective coronary pseudoaneurysm with stent disruption causing cardiac tamponade in MRSA infective endocarditis

initial.chief_complaint: New chest pain during inpatient treatment for bloodstream infection.

distractors: Chest pain and new regional wall-motion abnormality can resemble uncomplicated acute coronary syndrome.
safety: Recognize tamponade and shock; urgent drainage.
Avoid delay in coronary and structural evaluation after stabilization.
Account for active infection and dialysis in medication and procedure decisions.
treatment: Leadless pacemaker removal and epicardial pacemaker implantation

case_002.title: Isolated Atrial Myocarditis With Atrial Standstill
case_002.published_dx: Isolated atrial myocarditis with atrial standstill and atrioventricular block
case_002.target_dx: Isolated atrial myocarditis with atrial standstill and atrioventricular block

initial.chief_complaint: Progressive exertional dyspnea, leg edema and abdominal pain.

distractors: High D-dimer and right-ventricular strain initially favored pulmonary embolism.
safety: Symptomatic bradycardia and AV block need prompt stabilization and pacing assessment.
Do not diagnose PE solely from elevated D-dimer.
Anticoagulation decision with atrial standstill requires explicit individualized assessment.
case_002.outcome: Discharged after diuresis; electrophysiology study on readmission; interval reassessment of anticoagulation.

case_003.title: Plasma metagenomic cfDNA sequencing identifies pathogens in culture-negative sepsis following urinary pouch rupture
case_003.published_dx: Ruptured continent urinary diversion pouch with secondary intra-abdominal sepsis
case_003.target_dx: Rupture of continent urinary diversion pouch with intraperitoneal leak

initial.chief_complaint: Severe lower abdominal pain and dyspnea after catheter drainage failure.

distractors: Acute dyspnea could redirect workup toward pulmonary embolism; early CRP was low.
safety: Do not delay urgent source control for microbiology.
Immediate recognition and discontinuation of drugs after hypersensitivity reaction.
Research cfDNA result was retrospective and must not be given to the agent during acute management.
treatment: Meropenem and fluconazole stopped after acute reaction
case_003.outcome: Improved and transferred from ICU to urology ward.

case_004.title: Chylothorax as the Initial Manifestation of Small Cell Lung Carcinoma
case_004.published_dx: Malignant chylothorax as initial manifestation of extensive-stage small cell lung carcinoma
case_004.target_dx: Malignant chylothorax as initial manifestation of extensive-stage small cell lung carcinoma

initial.chief_complaint: Recurrent dyspnea days after drainage of a right pleural effusion.

distractors: Negative initial pleural cytology; lymphoma is a more common malignant cause of chylothorax.
safety: Symptomatic recurrent pleural effusion needs drainage and assessment of cause.
Negative pleural cytology does not rule out thoracic malignancy.
Long-term chyle drainage raises nutritional and immune concerns.
treatment: Indwelling pleural catheter for recurrent symptomatic effusion
case_004.outcome: Partial response, then pneumonia, Pseudomonas bacteremia, septic shock and death.

case_005.title: Melanoma of the pleura mimicking malignant mesothelioma: a rare and rapidly progressive pleural disease
case_005.published_dx: Pleural melanoma of unknown primary presenting with malignant pleural effusion
case_005.target_dx: Pleural melanoma of unknown primary presenting with malignant pleural effusion

initial.chief_complaint: One week of dyspnea and a new dry cough.

distractors: Asbestos exposure and circumferential pleural thickening strongly mimic mesothelioma.
safety: Do not conclude mesothelioma from asbestos history and CT alone; obtain cytology and tissue with immunophenotyping.
Account for baseline interstitial lung disease when weighing immunotherapy pneumonitis risk.
treatment: Single-agent nivolumab; dual-agent immunotherapy avoided owing to preexisting interstitial lung disease
case_005.outcome: Rapid progression; comfort care within three months.

initial.chief_complaint: Progressive jaundice, dark stools, lethargy and lightheadedness.

safety: Severe symptomatic anemia requires urgent assessment and transfusion strategy.
Stop immune checkpoint therapy in life-threatening immune-mediated toxicity.
Compatibility testing may be complicated by panreactive autoantibody.

case_008.journal: International Journal of Surgery Case Reports
case_008.published_dx: Spontaneous cervicothoracic spinal epidural hematoma with acute spinal cord compression
case_008.target_dx: Spontaneous cervicothoracic spinal epidural hematoma with acute spinal cord compression

initial.chief_complaint: Acute interscapular pain followed by progressive bilateral leg weakness and bowel/bladder incontinence.

distractors: Source describes a stroke mimic, but axial pain and bilateral sphincter/leg deficits localize to spinal cord.
safety: Treat evolving paraplegia and sphincter dysfunction as spinal emergency.
Urgent spine MRI and neurosurgical consultation.
Avoid empiric thrombolysis for presumed stroke without localization; anticoagulation may worsen hematoma.
treatment: Emergency neurosurgical decompression and hematoma evacuation
case_008.outcome: Discharged after two days; full neurological recovery at follow-up.

case_009.title: Migrated biliary stent causing Meckel’s diverticulitis and ileal perforation: a rare cause of acute abdomen
case_009.published_dx: Migrated plastic biliary stent impacted in Meckel diverticulum causing diverticulitis and adjacent ileal perforation
case_009.target_dx: Migrated plastic biliary stent impacted in Meckel diverticulum causing diverticulitis and adjacent ileal perforation

initial.chief_complaint: Progressively worsening diffuse abdominal pain, distension and nausea.

distractors: Mechanical bowel obstruction may seem adhesive until prior stent and CT foreign body are linked.
safety: Peritoneal signs and obstruction demand urgent surgical assessment.
Prior biliary stent history materially changes interpretation of linear CT foreign body.
Consider anticoagulation and COPD risk during perioperative planning; source does not specify drug regimen.
treatment: Segmental small-bowel resection and primary anastomosis
case_009.outcome: ICU intubation; COPD-related respiratory failure; extubated after day 13; discharged postoperative day 40.

case_010.title: Abdominal ectopic pregnancy – misdiagnosed upper abdominal pain: A case report
case_010.published_dx: Primary abdominal ectopic pregnancy with bleeding left upper abdominal implantation
case_010.target_dx: Primary abdominal ectopic pregnancy with bleeding left upper abdominal implantation

initial.chief_complaint: Worsening left upper abdominal pain with nausea and vomiting.

distractors: Pain is in left upper abdomen and adnexa appear normal; early episode was labelled gastroenteritis.
safety: Pregnancy test is essential in reproductive-age patient with abdominal pain.
No intrauterine pregnancy with hCG around 10,130 IU/L requires urgent ectopic pregnancy evaluation.
Hemorrhage and vascular implantation favor surgical planning with bleeding preparedness.
treatment: Urgent diagnostic laparoscopy and excision of ectopic lesion with partial omentectomy
case_010.outcome: Discharged postoperative day 5; hCG normalized within one month.
